purpose: Execute the most current next gates: phallic mandrel forensics, modular Osiris/genital attachment, female-genital mirror search, and royal biological-sex control, while keeping the Mendes CG 53465-53469 concordance as the primary archive blocker.
claim_ceiling: No test in this batch identifies a literal Osiris relic, reconstructs Osiris anatomy, proves a shared mold, proves a hidden-female Osiris/Seth hypothesis, or proves a ceremonial phallus-detachment event.

PHALLIC_MANDREL_FORENSICS_PASS.reason: No two current objects share the same construction class/material family while also exposing sufficient genital-specific metrology. Overall size similarity alone would not establish a shared mold even if more dimensions were available.

evidence.finding: Osiris penis and testicles were made separately and inserted into an oval recess in the body.
Curved terracotta phallus made for insertion into a mould-made figure; length 6.60 cm, thickness 1.70 cm.
Figure had a large separately made phallus inserted into a hole; only a stump remains, fixed with plaster.
Ptolemaic Egyptian figure preserves an empty socket for a removable phallus.

MODULAR_OSIRIS_GENITAL_ATTACHMENT_PASS.conclusion: Separately manufactured, inserted/removable phalli are a real Egyptian object technology, and an Osiris-specific example is directly documented. A removable component can also be lost or survive only as a stump/socket in other figures.
MODULAR_OSIRIS_GENITAL_ATTACHMENT_PASS.not_established: No evidence currently ties a mechanical failure during a ceremony to the origin of the Osiris missing-phallus myth.

mendes_evidence.finding: Grand Egyptian Museum records a Ptolemaic Hathor capital excavated at Mendes/Tell el-Ruba in 1892-1893.
Metropolitan Museum describes the Mendesian triad as Banebdjedet, goddess Hatmehyt and child god Harpocrates.
British Museum curatorial notes cite 5th-3rd century BCE Mendes parallels for nude female shrine plaques of the Isis-Hathor class.

general_female_genital_controls: Met cowrie/cowroid objects explicitly associated with resemblance to female genitalia and fertility
Egyptian female fertility figurines emphasizing pubic/genital area
Naukratis Ptolemaic terracotta women exposing/indicating the genital region
FEMALE_GENITAL_MIRROR_PROVENANCE_PASS.result: The mirrored search is not empty: Mendes contains substantial female divine/fertility symbolism. However no secure Mendes gold vulva/female-genital cover counterpart was located in the current pass.
FEMALE_GENITAL_MIRROR_PROVENANCE_PASS.next: Search Mendes excavation publications and museum distribution records for female figurines, cowries/cowroids, Hathor/Isis plaques, pubic-triangle objects and female genital covers using the same provenance rules applied to phallic objects.

ROYAL_MUMMY_BIOLOGICAL_SEX_AUDIT.result: No confirmed case in the checked royal set has yet been found where an accepted male pharaoh mummy was scientifically reclassified as biologically female.
ROYAL_MUMMY_BIOLOGICAL_SEX_AUDIT.priority_effect: Keep open as a falsification control, but lower immediate priority relative to the Mendes object/provenance gates.

MENDES_CG53465_53469_CONCORDANCE.result: The five Cairo Catalogue General records remain unresolved at individual-object level in public indexing.
MENDES_CG53465_53469_CONCORDANCE.next: Object-card/OCR extraction or an authorized museum records request remains necessary before the Mendes gold sheath can be assigned an exact CG number.
